## Summary

MNSUAM operates a comprehensive enterprise-grade wireless network infrastructure managed through a Cisco 3500 Series Wireless LAN Controller (WLC), providing campus-wide Wi-Fi connectivity to all academic, administrative, residential, and research facilities. This ICT infrastructure directly supports the university's sustainability mission by enabling digital operations, remote access to LMS, paperless administration, smart energy monitoring (including the solar EMIS dashboard), and data-driven decision-making across campus.

## Campus Wi-Fi Infrastructure — Key Statistics (June 3, 2026)

| # | Parameter | Value | Significance |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wireless Controller | Cisco 3500 Series WLC | Enterprise-grade, centrally managed |
| 2 | Total Access Points (APs) | 96 APs (75 operational) | Campus-wide coverage |
| 3 | Total Active Clients | 1,321–1,348 concurrent users | High-density digital campus |
| 4 | Number of SSIDs / WLANs | 6 dedicated networks | Role-based access control |
| 5 | Top WLAN by Clients | Faculty: 872 clients | Largest user group |
| 6 | Student Network Clients | 363 active students | E-learning support |
| 7 | AP Models Deployed | AIR-AP3802, AIR-AP8321, AIR-AP1832I | 802.11ac Wave 2 capable |
| 8 | Monitoring System | Real-time WLC dashboard (live) | Continuous ICT monitoring |
| 9 | Dual-Band Coverage | 2.4 GHz + 5 GHz | High capacity & low interference |
| 10 | Connected Device Types | Intel (64%), Hon Hai (14%), Samsung (5%), Apple (3%)... | Multi-platform support |

## How this ICT infrastructure supports sustainability

The campus-wide Wi-Fi enables paperless administration across all 6 departments, remote access to the university's LMS (reducing commuting needs), real-time monitoring of the solar EMIS dashboard, digital sustainability reporting, and online collaboration through Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 — all directly reducing the university's carbon footprint.
